evidence_quotes.two_concerns_question: Not asked. Rep opened with 'before I proceed, I just wanted to check if you have concerns or any important things' but this is a generic check-in, not the two-concerns template about movers showing up on time or damage.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer raised transparency/pricing concern upfront. Rep acknowledged but moved immediately to logistics gathering without probing deeper ('tell me more about that'). No real second layer.
evidence_quotes.value_days: Never addressed. Rep gave a flat estimate of $3,415 for 8.5 hours with no mention of day-of-week pricing or date flexibility.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_then_ask: Rep never asked for the business. After the customer expressed price objection ('this goes a little bit very high'), rep asked 'Do you still want me to send you the email quotation' and the call drifted to a soft close. No ask like 'Would you like our help with your move?' No rate lock or no-deposit language either.

top_strength: Rep gathered detailed logistics systematically (addresses, floor levels, walking distances, specific furniture items, box count estimate) and disclosed the all-inclusive pricing model and no-hidden-fees commitment clearly, which addressed the customer's stated transparency concern.
coaching_note: Step 2 is missing entirely — the two-concerns question (movers on time vs. damage) never landed, so you didn't anchor to what the customer actually worries about before jumping into probing; and you never asked for the business in step 7, so even though you built a quote, there was no close and no chance to lock the rate or confirm a booking.
